glossary.def: Hidden thinking tokens a reasoning model produces before its visible answer. They are billed as output tokens and count against the output cap.
The authority order in the OpenAI Model Spec: Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, then No Authority for assistant and tool messages and quoted or untrusted text.
Text from tools, files, images or quoted blocks that carries no authority by default. Instructions inside it are information, not commands.
A release check that runs a golden set against a candidate bundle of prompt, model and settings and blocks the release on regressions.
Copying live requests to a candidate version and comparing its output without serving it to users.
A tool that searches for better instructions, examples, tool descriptions or models against a metric on a dataset, such as DSPy compilers or the Foundry agent optimizer.
A serving technique that adds and removes requests from a running batch at each step, which keeps GPUs busy. vLLM uses it with PagedAttention.
An approved Azure OpenAI setting that removes storage of prompts and completions for abuse review, along with human review.
A network interface in your virtual network that reaches a service over a private IP, so traffic does not cross the public internet.
Choosing the relevant tables, columns, descriptions and sample values to show the model before it writes SQL.
Database enforcement of which rows a caller can read or write, using filter and block predicates, so it applies to any SQL including model-generated SQL.
The caller-defined string that selects an Azure Container Apps dynamic session. Treat it as sensitive and scope it to one user or tenant.
A model operating a browser or desktop by reading screenshots and proposing clicks and keystrokes that your app executes in an isolated environment.
A long-horizon agent that plans, searches many sources in parallel, reads them and writes a cited report, usually in a background run.
A RunFinished outcome that pauses an agent for human input. The client resumes by starting a new run whose input carries a resume array.
Output that contradicts the source or supplied context.
Output that cannot be verified from the source or supplied context.
Output that conflicts with real-world facts. Huang et al. contrast it with faithfulness, where output is inconsistent with instructions, context or its own logic.

claims.text: OpenAI reasoning.effort values are model-dependent and can include none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. gpt-5.5 defaults to medium.
GPT-6 Astra rejects effort none with HTTP 400. GPT-6.1 Sol rejects none and minimal. Chat Completions does not support function calling on either model.
OpenAI recommends reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output when starting, and hitting max_output_tokens gives status incomplete, possibly before visible output.
Claude effort is set with output_config.effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), default high on most models and medium on Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5.
Manual budget_tokens is deprecated on Claude 4.6 and returns HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7 and later.

Snell et al. (2024-08) report more than 4x efficiency over best-of-N and a smaller model beating a 14x larger one in a FLOPs-matched comparison. s1 (2025-01) budget forcing raised AIME24 from 50% to 57%.
The OpenAI Model Spec version dated 2026-08-18 orders authority Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, then No Authority (assistant and tool messages, quoted or untrusted text, multimodal data).

In the Model Spec, quoted text, files, images and tool outputs have no authority by default unless an unquoted higher-level instruction delegates it, a later message at the same level supersedes an earlier one, and the spec says production models do not yet fully reflect it.
In OpenAI's API, developer messages carry rules and business logic and user messages carry inputs. The instructions parameter takes priority over input.

OpenAI recommends pinning production to specific model snapshots and versioning prompts in code. Reusable prompt objects are being deprecated: prompt creation is de-emphasized from 2026-06-03 and v1/prompts is scheduled to shut down on 2026-11-30.

Azure Architecture Center: test changes to model version, prompt, configuration, orchestration and retrieval, and pin tested combinations. Retired deployments return HTTP errors, and deprecated ones accept no new deployments but keep working until retirement.

OpenAI's dataset-backed prompt optimizer and Evals platform are read-only for existing users on 2026-10-31 with shutdown scheduled for 2026-11-30, and the docs warn optimized prompts can perform worse on specific inputs.

The Foundry agent optimizer improves instructions, function-calling tool descriptions and model selection for prompt agents, and also skills for hosted agents. A prompt-agent candidate can be promoted to a new version.
The Foundry agent optimizer invokes the agent on every dataset task, so external tool calls execute. Prompt-agent function tools run client side and their execution is not evaluated.
The Foundry agent optimizer is a preview feature as of 2026-10-13. UNVERIFIED: the Learn page text fetched that day did not state GA or preview, and the status comes from the reference record.
The agent optimizer pre-run cost estimate is modeled from static token assumptions and is not a spending limit.

In the DSPy paper compiled pipelines beat standard few-shot prompting by over 25% (GPT-3.5) and 65% (llama2-13b-chat). MIPRO beat baselines on 5 of 7 programs by up to 13% with Llama-3-8B. GEPA beat GRPO by 6% on average and up to 20% with up to 35x fewer rollouts.
The vLLM paper reports 2 to 4x throughput at the same latency against prior systems. SGLang reports up to 6.4x throughput and uses RadixAttention and compressed finite state machines.

KAITO on AKS is a CNCF Sandbox project integrating vLLM and needs NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or later (no T4 or V100), Azure CLI 2.76.0 or later, no Windows node pools and public Azure regions only.

Foundry deployment types: Global may run inference in any region, Data Zone stays in the US, EU or APAC zone, Standard and Regional Provisioned stay in the geography. Global Batch and Data Zone Batch give a 50% discount, and the Developer tier has no SLA or residency guarantee.

Under OpenAI ZDR, store on /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions is treated as false, abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default, and threads, vector stores and fine-tuning jobs are not ZDR eligible.
Foundry customer-managed keys use Key Vault or Managed HSM, cover data at rest in associated storage, need RSA keys of at least 2048 bits and follow the latest key version when keyVersion is omitted.
Under Foundry network isolation, browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are not supported, and Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints.
OpenAI background mode retains response data for about 10 minutes, which conflicts with Zero Data Retention.
BIRD: ChatGPT reached 40.08% execution accuracy against 92.96% for humans. Spider 2.0: an o1-preview code agent solved 21.3%, against 91.2% on Spider 1.0 and 73.0% on BIRD.
The P2SQL paper shows unsanitized prompts can drive SQL injection in LangChain-based LLM-integrated web apps.

SQL Server and Azure SQL row-level security uses filter predicates (silently filter SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE) and block predicates, and a middle tier can set a user id in SESSION_CONTEXT with @read_only to stop changes until the connection returns to the pool.

Azure Container Apps code interpreter sessions use a Hyper-V boundary, a caller-defined session identifier that is sensitive, up to 600 concurrent sessions, idle cooldown of 300 to 3600 seconds and EgressDisabled by default. Doc samples use api-version 2025-10-02-preview.
The Foundry Code Interpreter has charges beyond token fees, creates a session per simultaneous conversation, and each session is active one hour by default with a 30-minute idle timeout.
The Foundry computer use tool is preview, has no SLA, is not recommended for production, uses the computer-use-preview model and is not supported in network-isolated Foundry.

Claude computer_toolset_20260801 is GA on the Claude API and Google Cloud and beta on Microsoft Foundry and Bedrock. Claude 5.5 and later reject computer_20251124 and computer_20250124 on the Claude API.
For GPT-6 Astra OpenAI recommends code execution (Playwright or PyAutoGUI) for computer use, and the computer tool remains supported as an alternative.

OpenAI deep research models need at least one data source, a remote MCP server must expose search and fetch with require_approval never, file search allows at most two vector stores, and the API has no clarification or prompt-rewriting step. The deprecation notice lists 2026-07-23 shutdown with gpt-5.6-sol as replacement.

The Foundry Deep Research tool is deprecated, the page cites 2026-11-19 for o3-deep-research retirement on Azure, and the old tool needed 2025-05-15-preview, West US or Norway East and Grounding with Bing.

Anthropic reports about 4x tokens for agents and about 15x for multi-agent versus chat, token usage explaining 80% of BrowseComp variance, and a 90.2% gain over single-agent Opus 4 on its internal eval.

AG-UI RunStarted and either RunFinished or RunError are mandatory. A RunFinished with outcome interrupt pauses for human input and the client resumes with a new run carrying a resume array. StateDelta uses JSON Patch (RFC 6902).
AG-UI is transport agnostic (SSE, webhooks, WebSockets) and the HttpAgent client supports HTTP SSE and a binary protocol.

The same text can differ up to 15x in token count across languages with 2023 tokenizers and byte-level models still show over 4x differences. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 split digits into 1 to 3 digit chunks left to right, and right-to-left grouping with commas improved arithmetic.
Huang et al. split hallucination into factuality and faithfulness. The 2025-09 paper Why Language Models Hallucinate argues benchmarks that reward guessing over abstaining keep errors alive.

Anthropic advises finding the simplest solution possible and increasing complexity only when needed. The Azure Architecture Center advises the lowest level of complexity that reliably meets requirements.
